notes: Replaced migrate-business-case-estimation with migrate-assessment-cost-estimation because current Azure Migrate business-case documentation marks that feature Preview. The CAF sequencing fact uses Secure as the documented example of work spanning adoption phases.

cards.statement: Azure can evict Azure Spot Virtual Machines during a running batch job when it needs the capacity.
cards.explanation: Azure Spot Virtual Machines use spare capacity that Azure can reclaim during execution. A batch design needs to tolerate interruption and recover unfinished work.

cards.statement: Azure Dedicated Host gives a regulated workload exclusive use of the datacenter's physical network.
cards.explanation: Azure Dedicated Host isolates the physical compute server. Its network and underlying storage infrastructure remain shared with other hosts.
cards.misconception: Dedicated compute hardware also provides a customer-exclusive physical datacenter network.

cards.statement: Azure Container Apps lets platform teams directly manage deployments through the Kubernetes API.
cards.explanation: Azure Container Apps abstracts the Kubernetes API. A requirement for direct Kubernetes API access points to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS).
cards.misconception: The managed Kubernetes foundation of Azure Container Apps exposes its Kubernetes API to customers.

source.title: Comparing Container Apps with other Azure container options

cards.statement: Azure CNI Overlay conserves virtual network addresses by assigning AKS pods a separate address range.
cards.explanation: Azure CNI Overlay assigns pod addresses from a range separate from the node subnet. This reduces the virtual network address space a large AKS deployment consumes.

source.title: CNI networking in Azure Kubernetes Service

cards.statement: Azure Container Instances can provide full orchestration for applications needing coordinated multi-container scaling.
cards.explanation: Azure Container Instances runs containers rather than supplying a full orchestration platform. A coordinated scaling requirement needs another orchestration design.
cards.misconception: Azure Container Instances includes the orchestration needed for a coordinated container application.

cards.statement: An App Service Environment can host isolated web applications directly inside an organization's Azure virtual network.
cards.explanation: App Service Environment deploys managed application hosting within a customer's virtual network, providing network isolation for web workloads.

cards.statement: Azure Functions Premium can end its compute charges by releasing its idle plan's remaining instances.
cards.explanation: An active Azure Functions Premium plan retains a minimum billed allocation even when its apps are idle. Budgeting must account for that standing compute cost.
cards.misconception: Azure Functions Premium scales its active plan to zero billed compute during idle periods.

cards.statement: Azure Functions Flex Consumption can reach private dependencies through virtual network integration.
cards.explanation: Flex Consumption connects function apps to services secured within a virtual network, meeting private-resource access requirements within its serverless hosting model.

source.title: Azure Functions Flex Consumption plan hosting

cards.statement: The Azure Functions Premium plan supports custom Linux containers for workloads with packaged dependencies.
cards.explanation: The Premium plan accepts custom Linux container deployments, so the workload can bring the runtime environment its dependencies need.

cards.statement: Azure Functions lets an architect extend the HTTP response deadline by increasing the function execution timeout.
cards.explanation: Azure Functions enforces an HTTP response limit separately from execution timeout. Long processing can use an asynchronous response pattern instead.
cards.misconception: A longer function execution timeout also lengthens the HTTP request's response window.
cards.volatilityNote: HTTP response limits and their relationship to execution timeouts can change with Azure Functions hosting.

cards.statement: Microsoft recommends Azure CycleCloud when HPC jobs need to retain scheduler-specific scripts and policies.
cards.explanation: Azure CycleCloud preserves an existing scheduler operating model while provisioning Azure infrastructure, avoiding a rewrite into another scheduling model.

cards.statement: Azure Batch adds a scheduling-service charge to the compute resources a parallel processing workload consumes.
cards.explanation: Azure Batch charges for underlying resources such as compute, storage, and networking. The Batch scheduling service adds no separate charge.
cards.misconception: Azure Batch adds a separate service fee for managing job scheduling.

cards.statement: Azure Service Bus requires sessions to guarantee FIFO processing within a workflow's related message groups.
cards.explanation: Azure Service Bus sessions keep related messages under one receiver's exclusive lock. This enables ordered processing of a workflow's message sequence.

cards.statement: Azure Event Hubs supports a global arrival order guarantee across partitions for a partitioned telemetry stream.
cards.explanation: Ordering in Azure Event Hubs applies within a partition. An architect keeps related events in the same partition when processing depends on their arrival order.
cards.misconception: Azure Event Hubs preserves arrival order across separate partitions.

cards.statement: Azure Event Grid subject filters let a subscriber select blob events from a chosen container in a storage account.
cards.explanation: Azure Event Grid uses the event subject's container path to filter storage events before delivering them to a subscriber.

source.title: Event filtering in Azure Event Grid

cards.statement: Azure Storage queues automatically move repeatedly failing messages into a built-in dead-letter queue.
cards.explanation: A consumer of Azure Storage queues checks a message's DequeueCount and implements its own policy for moving poison messages to a dead-letter queue.
cards.misconception: Azure Storage queues provide automatic poison-message isolation.

source.title: Storage queues and Service Bus queues compared and contrasted

cards.statement: Azure API Management Premium supports gateways in multiple Azure regions within the same service instance.
cards.explanation: Azure API Management Premium deploys regional gateways for geographically distributed callers. Its management plane remains in the primary region.
cards.volatilityNote: Azure API Management tier capabilities evolve as v2 offerings gain features.

source.title: Deploy an Azure API Management instance to multiple Azure regions

cards.statement: A running Azure API Management self-hosted gateway stops serving APIs when its connection to Azure fails.
cards.explanation: A running Azure API Management self-hosted gateway continues using its in-memory configuration during a temporary Azure connection loss. Configuration updates and cloud telemetry pause.
cards.misconception: A self-hosted gateway requires continuous cloud connectivity to process API traffic.

cards.statement: Azure Managed Redis automatically rebuilds an in-memory cache from enabled persistence after node failures.
cards.explanation: Persistence restores the same Azure Managed Redis cache from its latest persisted state. Recovery can lose writes that have not yet reached persistence.

source.title: Configure data persistence for an Azure Managed Redis instance

cards.statement: Azure App Configuration stores different values for the same key by using environment labels.
cards.explanation: Azure App Configuration identifies values by the combination of key and label. Environment labels let applications select their own variant from a shared store.

source.title: Understand Azure App Configuration key-value store

cards.statement: Azure App Configuration can copy a secret's value into its store through a Key Vault reference.
cards.explanation: Azure App Configuration stores a URI for a Key Vault reference. The application authenticates to Azure Key Vault and retrieves the secret's value.
cards.misconception: A Key Vault reference duplicates the secret inside Azure App Configuration.

source.title: Use Key Vault references in an ASP.NET Core app

cards.statement: A template spec's read permission allows a release team to deploy its resources to a target resource group.
cards.explanation: A release team needs deployment permissions at the target scope in addition to read access to the template spec.
cards.misconception: Template spec access grants permission to deploy its described resources.

cards.statement: Azure deployment stacks can relinquish management of a resource that an operations team intends to keep running.
cards.explanation: An architect selects detachment when removing a resource from a deployment stack's template. Azure keeps the resource and removes it from the stack's managed set.

source.title: Create and deploy Azure deployment stacks in Bicep

cards.statement: Azure Resource Manager preserves omitted properties when an incremental template includes an existing resource.
cards.explanation: An incremental Azure Resource Manager deployment reapplies an included resource's properties. Omitted properties can reset to defaults, so the template describes the intended final state.
cards.misconception: An incremental deployment merges supplied properties into an existing resource while retaining omitted values.

cards.statement: An architect uses the Cloud Adoption Framework's Ready phase to design the Azure landing zone for adoption.
cards.explanation: Ready establishes platform guardrails and workload environments that give migration teams an Azure destination aligned with organizational requirements.

source.title: What is an Azure landing zone?

cards.statement: The Cloud Adoption Framework delays Secure work until an organization completes the Adopt phase.
cards.explanation: The Secure methodology applies across the Cloud Adoption Framework, including strategy, planning, readiness, and adoption. Teams integrate security during adoption.
cards.misconception: An organization completes workload adoption before it begins the Cloud Adoption Framework's security work.

cards.statement: Azure Migrate can estimate post-migration compute and storage costs from its Azure VM sizing recommendations.
cards.explanation: An Azure VM assessment calculates estimated running costs after it establishes readiness and sizing. Architects use this projection when comparing migration designs.

cards.statement: Azure Migrate Collector collects a discovery snapshot in an on-premises network with restricted Azure connectivity.
cards.explanation: The Collector scans the estate locally and exports inventory for later upload. Discovery therefore suits environments where continuous Azure connectivity is impractical.
cards.volatilityNote: The Collector's supported discovery environments can expand.

source.title: Discover servers and workloads using Azure Migrate collector

cards.statement: For VMware vSphere, Azure Migrate uses guest-installed migration agents when it reuses its discovery appliance.
cards.explanation: The VMware vSphere migration path using the discovery appliance is agentless. Replication proceeds through VMware snapshots and changed block tracking instead of guest agents.
cards.misconception: The migration path that reuses Azure Migrate's discovery appliance still needs migration agents inside VMware guest VMs.

cards.statement: Azure Migrate uses provider agents on Hyper-V hosts to migrate their virtual machines to Azure.
cards.explanation: Azure Migrate's Hyper-V replication provider runs on hosts or cluster nodes. An architect plans host-level installation for this migration path.

cards.statement: Azure Database Migration Service in the Azure portal supports online migration to Azure SQL Database.
cards.explanation: The Azure portal version of Azure Database Migration Service provides an offline migration path to Azure SQL Database. The migration design accounts for downtime.
cards.misconception: The Azure portal version of Azure Database Migration Service provides an online path for Azure SQL Database.
cards.volatilityNote: The service's supported migration paths can expand.

source.title: What is Azure Database Migration Service?

cards.statement: An architect can run a built-in compatibility assessment with Azure Database Migration Service in the portal.
cards.explanation: The portal comparison table lists source assessment as unsupported by Azure Database Migration Service. Architects use a separate assessment capability before migration.
cards.misconception: Azure Database Migration Service in the portal includes built-in source compatibility assessments.
cards.volatilityNote: Portal assessment capabilities may change as Azure Database Migration Service evolves.

source.title: What is Azure Database Migration Service?

cards.statement: Azure SQL Database retains TDE protection inside a BACPAC file exported for a database migration.
cards.explanation: Exporting a TDE-protected Azure SQL Database produces an unencrypted BACPAC. A migration design needs separate protection for that exported data.
cards.misconception: TDE encryption follows the database data into its exported BACPAC file.

cards.statement: Azure Storage Mover can catch up on-premises file changes after Azure Data Box seeds the migration target.
cards.explanation: Storage Mover compares the local source with the seeded target and transfers differences before cutover, shrinking the final online transfer.

cards.statement: Azure Data Box moves bulk data to Azure when limited WAN bandwidth makes an online transfer impractical.
cards.explanation: Data Box carries bulk data physically to an Azure datacenter, reducing dependence on the WAN link for the migration.

cards.statement: AzCopy automatically preserves source blob index tags when it copies blobs between Azure storage accounts.
cards.explanation: An architect retaining blob index tags during an AzCopy migration reapplies them to the destination blobs. The copy operation does not preserve them automatically.
cards.misconception: AzCopy carries blob index tags into the destination as part of its default copy behavior.
cards.volatilityNote: AzCopy's metadata and tag preservation behavior can change between versions.

source.title: Copy blobs between Azure storage accounts by using AzCopy

cards.statement: Azure Front Door Standard and Premium can accelerate HTTP(S) applications distributed across Azure regions.
cards.explanation: Azure Front Door Standard and Premium use Microsoft's global edge network to accelerate delivery for applications with origins in different Azure regions.

cards.statement: Azure Traffic Manager can move an established client connection to another region when an endpoint fails.
cards.explanation: Traffic Manager influences DNS answers for subsequent connections. Clients connect directly to endpoints, so an existing connection recovers through client reconnection.
cards.misconception: Traffic Manager's regional failover transfers live client connections.

cards.statement: Azure Application Gateway's TLS listener passes the client's TLS session unchanged to the backend.
cards.explanation: A TLS listener terminates the client's TLS session at Application Gateway. The gateway creates a separate connection to the selected backend.
cards.misconception: Application Gateway's TLS proxy preserves the client-to-backend TLS session.

cards.statement: Azure Load Balancer routes public TCP and UDP workloads through a global endpoint across regional deployments.
cards.explanation: Azure Load Balancer's global topology fronts regional load balancers through a shared public endpoint for transport-layer traffic.

cards.statement: The ExpressRoute Premium add-on extends a circuit's Azure connectivity beyond its geopolitical region.
cards.explanation: ExpressRoute Premium adds connectivity across geopolitical boundaries, meeting a design that connects an on-premises network to more distant Azure deployments.

cards.statement: Azure Virtual WAN supports VPN-to-ExpressRoute branch transit through its Standard hubs.
cards.explanation: A Standard virtual WAN hub routes traffic between VPN and ExpressRoute spokes, meeting branch-to-branch connectivity needs when transit routing is enabled.

cards.statement: An Azure Private Link private endpoint automatically disables public network access to its target service.
cards.explanation: A private endpoint adds a private access path. The service owner configures public network access separately to meet an isolation requirement.
cards.misconception: Creating a private endpoint also closes the target service's public endpoint.

cards.statement: Azure virtual network service endpoints can authorize Azure service access for traffic originating on-premises.
cards.explanation: Service endpoints identify Azure virtual network subnets. On-premises requests need a different access design because they do not use that subnet identity.
cards.misconception: Service endpoints extend subnet authorization to on-premises traffic.

cards.statement: Azure Firewall Premium meets a requirement to inspect the payload of outbound HTTPS traffic.
cards.explanation: Azure Firewall Premium's TLS inspection acts as a forward proxy, decrypting outbound HTTPS before re-encrypting it for the destination.

cards.statement: Azure NAT Gateway automatically translates internet-bound traffic to fixed public IPs that partners can allowlist.
cards.explanation: NAT Gateway uses configured static public IP addresses or prefixes for outbound traffic. Partners can allowlist that predefined address set instead of individual workload addresses.

cards.statement: Azure Application Gateway WAF can inspect HTTP requests received through its TCP or TLS proxy listeners.
cards.explanation: Azure Application Gateway WAF v2 can host TCP/TLS proxy listeners, but those listeners bypass WAF inspection. Use HTTP(S) listeners to inspect web requests.
cards.misconception: A WAF-enabled gateway inspects HTTP payloads on its TCP/TLS proxy listeners.
cards.volatilityNote: Inspection support for TCP and TLS proxy listeners may expand as this capability evolves.

cards.statement: Enabling DDoS IP Protection on a public IP also protects other public IPs in the same virtual network.
cards.explanation: DDoS IP Protection applies to the public IP address where it is enabled. Other addresses need their own protection coverage even when they share a virtual network.
cards.misconception: IP-level DDoS protection spreads to neighboring public IPs in the virtual network.
